{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793100897387,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01SmtDSDzbhTDNLqjCxgTbnP","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Simple Cholesky decomposition (unblocked, column-oriented, OpenMP parallel)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// The factorization proceeds column by column. For column j, the diagonal\n// element is computed first (single thread), then all off-diagonal elements\n// L[i][j] (i > j) are computed in parallel. Each element's dot product is\n// accumulated in the same ascending-k order as the sequential algorithm, so\n// results are bit-for-bit identical to the sequential row-oriented version.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* const a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel shared(ok)\n    {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            // Diagonal element L[j][j] (sequential; O(j) work)\n            #pragma omp single\n            {\n                const double* const Lj = a + j * n;\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += Lj[k] * Lj[k];\n                }\n                const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    ok = false;\n                } else {\n                    a[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n                }\n            }\n            // Implicit barrier after single: 'ok' is final for all threads here.\n            if (!ok) {\n                break;\n            }\n\n            const double Ljj = a[j * n + j];\n\n            // Off-diagonal elements of column j: independent across rows i\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t i = j + 1; i < n; ++i) {\n                const double* const Li = a + i * n;\n                const double* const Lj = a + j * n;\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += Li[k] * Lj[k];\n                }\n                a[i * n + j] = (a[i * n + j] - sum) / Ljj;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (!ok) {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Zero out upper triangular part\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            a[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B (sequential to keep the sequence deterministic)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T (rows are independent)\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    // Compute L * L^T (rows are independent)\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static) reduction(max : maxError, relError)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1793100897338,"end":1793100897376}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17d243d30001xSi4zqEerNQ6MZ","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","messageID":"msg_17d243008001KvlGkUz5BFPVR2"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793101024837,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"id":"prt_17d25e7f900115YfX1w3y16NG1","messageID":"msg_17d25e3da001IQjfbArNSbbtCu","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","type":"reasoning","text":"Oversubscribing to 256 threads hurts performance at small and medium n, likely due to hyperthreading contention and spin-waiting barrier overhead—clear at n=1000 (464ms) and n=2000 (976ms). This points to barrier synchronization cost scaling badly with thread count, so I should look at reducing barriers per column and cutting spin overhead.\n\nI could cap threads per problem size by requiring a minimum rows-per-thread ratio, but even then per-column work at n=2000 is only microseconds per thread, comparable to the barrier cost itself—it's really a granularity problem. A proper fix would be column blocking to amortize barriers, though that complicates the dependency structure; a simpler fix might be having each thread redundantly compute the diagonal element locally instead of using a \"single\" region, eliminating one barrier per column.\n\nSince prior-column entries are already finalized and barrier-protected, every thread can deterministically recompute the same diagonal value and failure check without coordination, then only one thread actually writes it back before the next barrier.\n\nBut I realize there's a subtle race: each thread reads the original a[j][j] value to compute its local diagonal check, yet the master thread may overwrite that same location with the sqrt result before other threads finish reading the original — I need to guard against this ordering issue.\n\nI think the cleanest fix is to have each thread read the original diagonal value before any writes happen, then synchronize with a barrier so all reads complete before the master updates the array in place.\n\nTracing through the indices, I confirm a[j][j] is only ever read as the divisor during the computation of column j itself, not by any later column's calculations—so there's no cross-column dependency on that diagonal value beyond its own column.\n\nFor each column j, every thread redundantly computes the same local value from the original diagonal entry minus the running sum, checks if it's non-positive to flag a failure, and I need to be careful that error printing only happens once rather than from every thread.\n\nSince each thread derives the identical value independently, having only the master thread print the error and others break silently keeps things consistent without needing an extra shared flag — though I still need a shared \"ok\" boolean for the caller to check after the parallel region ends. Then after the row loop finishes (barrier included), the master thread alone writes the square root into the diagonal entry, since the write must happen after all reads from that column are complete.\n\nI'm double-checking whether a[jj] is actually read anywhere beyond column j's own diagonal computation and divisor step, since that would determine whether deferring its write is safe.\n\nSince all threads perform identical deterministic arithmetic, their computed diagonal value will agree, so whichever thread detects a non-positive value and breaks, the result is consistent across threads—letting the master safely print the failure message first without needing extra synchronization on a shared flag.\n\nStill writing decomposition logic...\n\nThere's still just one barrier per column, so that's fine, and the redundant diagonal computation across threads is trivial compared to total work — negligible overhead even at scale. I should still test with 256 threads after this change, and if performance remains poor, consider capping the thread count so each thread handles a reasonable number of rows.\n\nLet me trace through the write/read ordering more carefully: the master's diagonal write in column j-1's epilogue is never read by other threads in column j's diagonal computation (which only reads off-diagonal entries), and it's also not read by other threads' column j omp-for work. Since nothing reads that value before the next barrier, there's no race there — the dependency ordering holds without needing extra synchronization.\n\n","time":{"start":1793100998650,"end":1793101024743},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793101024838,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"id":"prt_17d264def001FSc6pYTpcOZ3GU","messageID":"msg_17d25e3da001IQjfbArNSbbtCu","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","type":"text","text":"Two issues are visible. Nothing reads `A[j][j]` outside column j, so this is race-free.","time":{"start":1793101024751,"end":1793101024765}}}
{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793101028188,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_019X2yEjRYoJhk547boCWepM","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","oldString":"// Simple Cholesky decomposition (unblocked, column-oriented, OpenMP parallel)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// The factorization proceeds column by column. For column j, the diagonal\n// element is computed first (single thread), then all off-diagonal elements\n// L[i][j] (i > j) are computed in parallel. Each element's dot product is\n// accumulated in the same ascending-k order as the sequential algorithm, so\n// results are bit-for-bit identical to the sequential row-oriented version.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* const a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel shared(ok)\n    {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            // Diagonal element L[j][j] (sequential; O(j) work)\n            #pragma omp single\n            {\n                const double* const Lj = a + j * n;\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += Lj[k] * Lj[k];\n                }\n                const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    ok = false;\n                } else {\n                    a[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n                }\n            }\n            // Implicit barrier after single: 'ok' is final for all threads here.\n            if (!ok) {\n                break;\n            }\n\n            const double Ljj = a[j * n + j];\n\n            // Off-diagonal elements of column j: independent across rows i\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t i = j + 1; i < n; ++i) {\n                const double* const Li = a + i * n;\n                const double* const Lj = a + j * n;\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += Li[k] * Lj[k];\n                }\n                a[i * n + j] = (a[i * n + j] - sum) / Ljj;\n            }\n        }\n    }","newString":"// Simple Cholesky decomposition (unblocked, column-oriented, OpenMP parallel)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// The factorization proceeds column by column. Each element's dot\n// product is accumulated in the same ascending-k order as the sequential\n// algorithm, so results are bit-for-bit identical to the sequential version.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* const a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel shared(ok)\n    {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            // Diagonal element L[j][j]. Entry a[j][j] is only read in column j,\n            // and is published by the master thread after this column's barrier.\n            const double* const Lj = a + j * n;\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += Lj[k] * Lj[k];\n            }\n            const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite (all threads take this path together)\n                #pragma omp master\n                {\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    ok = false;\n                }\n                break;\n            }\n            const double Ljj = sqrt(val);\n\n            // Off-diagonal elements of column j: independent across rows i\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t i = j + 1; {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793101318019,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"id":"prt_17d2ac77d001D45qmNMo10OKPA","messageID":"msg_17d2ac133001Y2JBdcrTQfFNd2","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793101326139,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"id":"prt_17d2ac7800012VWzXdztFfgLEE","messageID":"msg_17d2ac133001Y2JBdcrTQfFNd2","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm trying to figure out why leaving OMP_NUM_THREADS unset gives 50ms while setting it to 32 gives 5ms — it seems like omp_get_max_threads() defaults to 256 when unset versus 32 explicitly, even though the actual team size used is 32 in both cases. I suspect libgomp's thread pool gets created with 256 threads on the first parallel region when unset, causing the slowdown.\n\nMy guess is that the matrix generation phase creates a pool of 256 threads, those threads spin-wait (governed by GOMP_SPINCOUNT/OMP_WAIT_POLICY) before going idle, and this spinning creates CPU contention with the subsequent 32-thread Cholesky step — even though idle threads should eventually sleep. It's possible affinity settings also play a role, though that seems less likely. I want to test by setting OMP_NUM_THREADS=256 explicitly for the generation phase to see if the same slowdown reproduces.\n\nTesting different thread counts confirms the pattern: t=128 gives 17ms, t=32 gives 5ms, t=16 gives 4-5ms — whenever the max thread count exceeds 32, things get slow, which fits the theory that the extra pool threads sit at a barrier waiting rather than actually spinning down cleanly. A practical fix would be capping thread counts uniformly across generation and validation phases rather than letting one phase spin up a much larger pool, but I want to first confirm by testing with OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive to see if that changes the behavior.\n\n","time":{"start":1793101318016,"end":1793101326077},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793101326140,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"id":"prt_17d2ae700001U4ciw1xMIJ3rhR","messageID":"msg_17d2ac133001Y2JBdcrTQfFNd2","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","type":"text","text":"The gap is real: with `OMP_NUM_THREADS` unset, the team is still 32 threads but takes ~50 ms, versus ~5 ms when the max is 32. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793101336256,"sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","part":{"id":"prt_17d2aef9e001Y6oJ50E25VVgKa","messageID":"msg_17d2aeb300016zA1dD3zLVjzYk","sessionID":"ses_e82dca3b0ffe64ooumI45Xy69R","type":"reasoning","text":"It's not just the wait policy then—the thread count seems to matter more. I'm wondering if this is about affinity settings, since leaving OMP_NUM_THREADS unset might trigger different OMP_PROC_BIND defaults than explicitly setting num_threads(32).\n\nActually the real culprit might be thread pool creation: with the env var unset, libgomp spins up 256 threads during the generation phase, while forcing 32 only creates 32 threads from the start. That leftover pool size from generation seems to carry over and affect the Cholesky decomposition timing regardless of what's explicitly requested afterward.\n\nOne fix is to call omp_set_num_threads globally before any parallel region runs, so the initial pool created during generation is already capped at 32 rather than 256.\n\nActually a cleaner approach: I'll define a small helper that computes an appropriate team size based on row count, and apply it consistently to every parallel region—generation, validation, and Cholesky alike—so the thread pool size is determined the same way everywhere and never balloons unnecessarily.\n\nI should check whether the unset env case drops to roughly 5ms, and for n=2000 the team size works out to about 125, which lines up with the earlier 128-thread measurement of ~46ms.\n\n","time":{"start":1793101328286,"end":1793101336180},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

For column j, every thread\n// redundantly computes the diagonal element L[j][j] (identical deterministic\n// arithmetic, O(j) work), then the off-diagonal elements L[i][j] (i > j) are\n// computed in parallel with a single barrier per column. Each element's dot\n// product is accumulated in the same ascending-k order as the sequential\n// algorithm, so results are bit-for-bit identical to the sequential version.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    double* const a = A.data();\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel num_threads(teamSize(n)) shared(ok)\n    {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            // Diagonal element L[j][j]. Entry a[j][j] is only read in column j,\n            // and is published by the master thread after this column's barrier.\n            const double* const Lj = a + j * n;\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += Lj[k] * Lj[k];\n            }\n            const double val = a[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite (all threads take this path together)\n                #pragma omp master\n                {\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    ok = false;\n                }\n                break;\n            }\n            const double Ljj = sqrt(val);\n\n            // Off-diagonal elements of column j: independent across rows i\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t i = j + 1; i < n; ++i) {\n                const double* const Li = a + i * n;\n                double s = 0.0;\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    s += Li[k] * Lj[k];\n                }\n                a[i * n + j] = (a[i * n + j] - s) / Ljj;\n            }\n\n            // All reads of a[j][j] in this column are complete (implicit barrier above)\n            #pragma omp master\n            {\n                a[j * n + j] = Ljj;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (!ok) {\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Zero out upper triangular part\n    #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(teamSize(n)) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0;
